title: Introduction to Computer Science 1
description: Introduction to programming and computational problem solving in Python. Covers variables, control flow, functions, recursion, lists and dictionaries, basic object-oriented programming and simple algorithm analysis.
learning_outcomes: Write and debug small Python programs; decompose problems into functions; use recursion and basic data structures; reason informally about running time.

title: Introduction to Computer Science 2
description: Second course in programming using Java. Object-oriented design, abstract data types, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, hash tables and heaps, with an introduction to asymptotic analysis of algorithms.
learning_outcomes: Implement core data structures in Java; choose a data structure for a task; analyse algorithms with big-O notation; apply OOP principles.

title: Combinatoric Structures
description: Mathematical foundations of computer science: logic, sets, functions, relations, proof techniques including induction, counting and combinatorics, graphs and discrete probability.
learning_outcomes: Write proofs by induction and contradiction; solve counting problems; reason about graphs and relations; apply discrete probability.

title: Computer Systems
description: How computers execute programs: data representation, C and assembly language, memory hierarchy and caches, linking, processes, and an introduction to operating system concepts.
learning_outcomes: Program in C and read assembly; explain number representation; reason about memory and caching; describe process and OS abstractions.

title: Introduction to the Analysis of Algorithms
description: Design and analysis of algorithms: greedy methods, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, graph algorithms, network flow, and NP-completeness.
learning_outcomes: Design algorithms with standard paradigms; prove correctness; analyse running time; recognise NP-complete problems.

title: Geometric Algorithms
description: Linear algebra through a computational lens: vectors, matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues, least squares, and applications to graphics, data and machine learning.
learning_outcomes: Solve linear systems; compute eigen-decompositions; apply linear algebra to geometric and data problems in code.

title: Algebraic Algorithms
description: Algebraic structures used in computing: modular arithmetic, groups, rings and fields, with applications to cryptography and error-correcting codes.
learning_outcomes: Apply number theory and abstract algebra to RSA, hashing and coding; implement algebraic algorithms.

title: Probability in Computing
description: Probability for computer scientists: discrete and continuous random variables, expectation, variance, concentration bounds, Markov chains, and randomized algorithms.
learning_outcomes: Model computing problems probabilistically; compute expectations and tail bounds; analyse randomized algorithms.

title: Concepts of Programming Languages
description: Programming language concepts: syntax, semantics, type systems, functional programming, interpreters, and comparison of language paradigms.
learning_outcomes: Implement an interpreter; reason about types and scope; program in a functional style.

title: Elements of the Theory of Computation
description: Theory of computation: finite automata, regular languages, context-free grammars, Turing machines, decidability and complexity classes.
learning_outcomes: Construct automata and grammars; prove languages non-regular; prove undecidability; reason about P and NP.

title: Fundamentals of Computing Systems
description: Fundamentals of computing systems: performance modelling, queueing, concurrency, synchronization, scheduling and resource management in operating systems.
learning_outcomes: Model system performance; write concurrent programs; analyse scheduling and synchronization.

title: Introductory Microeconomic Analysis
description: Introductory microeconomics: supply and demand, consumer and producer behaviour, market structures, market failure and the role of government.
learning_outcomes: Use supply-and-demand models; analyse firm behaviour across market structures; evaluate policy interventions.

title: Introductory Macroeconomic Analysis
description: Introductory macroeconomics: GDP, unemployment, inflation, economic growth, money and banking, and monetary and fiscal policy.
learning_outcomes: Interpret macroeconomic indicators; use AD-AS models; explain monetary and fiscal policy effects.

title: Intermediate Microeconomic Analysis
description: Intermediate microeconomic theory using calculus: consumer choice, production and cost, general equilibrium, game theory and welfare.
learning_outcomes: Solve constrained optimisation problems; derive demand and supply; analyse strategic interaction.

title: Intermediate Macroeconomic Analysis
description: Intermediate macroeconomic theory: long-run growth models, business cycles, IS-LM and AD-AS frameworks, open-economy macroeconomics and policy.
learning_outcomes: Build and solve growth and business-cycle models; evaluate stabilisation policy.

title: Empirical Economics 1
description: Empirical economics 1: probability, sampling distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing and simple regression with economic data.
learning_outcomes: Conduct hypothesis tests; estimate and interpret simple regressions; use statistical software.

title: Empirical Economics 2
description: Empirical economics 2: multiple regression, causal inference, instrumental variables, panel data and differences-in-differences, with an applied research project.
learning_outcomes: Estimate multivariate models; identify causal effects; complete an empirical project.

title: General Psychology
description: Survey of psychology: research methods, biological bases of behaviour, perception, learning, memory, development, personality, social behaviour and psychological disorders.
learning_outcomes: Describe major areas of psychology; explain basic research methods; apply concepts to everyday behaviour.

title: Experimental Design in Psychology
description: Experimental design in psychology: formulating hypotheses, designing experiments, controlling variables, ethics, data collection and analysis, and writing APA-style lab reports. Includes a lab component.
learning_outcomes: Design and run an experiment; analyse data with t-tests and ANOVA; write an APA-style research report.

title: Physiological Psychology
description: Physiological psychology: neurons, neurotransmission, brain anatomy, sensory and motor systems, sleep, motivation, emotion, learning and memory from a biological perspective.
learning_outcomes: Explain neural signalling; relate brain systems to behaviour; evaluate biological research methods.

title: Perception and Behavior
description: Perception and behaviour: sensory transduction, visual and auditory perception, psychophysics, attention and perceptual organisation.
learning_outcomes: Explain perceptual processes; apply psychophysical methods; relate perception to behaviour.

title: Introduction to Cognitive Psychology
description: Introduction to cognitive psychology: attention, memory, language, problem solving, reasoning and decision making.
learning_outcomes: Explain models of memory and attention; evaluate cognitive experiments; apply theories to real-world cognition.

title: Developmental Psychology
description: Developmental psychology across the lifespan: physical, cognitive, social and emotional development from infancy through adulthood.
learning_outcomes: Describe developmental stages and theories; evaluate developmental research designs.

title: Psychology of Personality: Theories and Application
description: Psychology of personality: trait, psychodynamic, humanistic and social-cognitive theories; personality assessment and applications.
learning_outcomes: Compare personality theories; evaluate assessment methods; apply theory to case material.

title: Social Psychology
description: Social psychology: attitudes, persuasion, conformity, group processes, prejudice, attraction and prosocial behaviour.
learning_outcomes: Explain core social-psychological phenomena; evaluate classic and modern studies.

title: Psychopathology
description: Psychopathology: classification, causes and treatment of psychological disorders including anxiety, mood, psychotic and personality disorders.
learning_outcomes: Describe DSM classification; explain aetiology models; compare treatment approaches.

title: Biology 1
description: Biology 1: chemistry of life, cell structure and function, metabolism, cell division, Mendelian and molecular genetics. Includes laboratory.
learning_outcomes: Explain cell structure and metabolism; solve genetics problems; perform basic lab techniques.

title: Biology 2
description: Biology 2: evolution, biodiversity, plant and animal physiology, and ecology. Includes laboratory.
learning_outcomes: Explain evolutionary mechanisms; describe organismal physiology; analyse ecological data.

title: Cell Biology
description: Cell biology: membranes, organelles, protein trafficking, cytoskeleton, cell signalling and the cell cycle.
learning_outcomes: Explain cellular processes at molecular level; interpret experimental cell-biology data.

title: Genetics
description: Genetics: Mendelian inheritance, linkage and mapping, chromosome biology, gene regulation, mutation and population genetics.
learning_outcomes: Solve transmission and mapping problems; explain gene regulation; apply population-genetics models.

title: General Chemistry 1
description: General chemistry 1: atomic structure, stoichiometry, chemical bonding, gases, thermochemistry and periodic trends. Includes laboratory.
learning_outcomes: Perform stoichiometric calculations; explain bonding and periodic trends; carry out lab measurements.

title: General Chemistry 2
description: General chemistry 2: kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, thermodynamics and electrochemistry. Includes laboratory.
learning_outcomes: Solve equilibrium and kinetics problems; apply thermodynamics; analyse electrochemical cells.

title: Organic Chemistry 1
description: Organic chemistry 1: structure, bonding, stereochemistry, nomenclature, substitution and elimination reactions. Includes laboratory.
learning_outcomes: Name organic compounds; predict reaction mechanisms; perform organic lab techniques.

title: Organic Chemistry 2
description: Organic chemistry 2: aromatic compounds, carbonyl chemistry, spectroscopy and multistep synthesis. Includes laboratory.
learning_outcomes: Interpret NMR and IR spectra; plan multistep syntheses.

title: Calculus I
description: Calculus I: limits, continuity, derivatives and their applications, and an introduction to integrals.
learning_outcomes: Compute limits and derivatives; solve optimisation and related-rates problems; evaluate basic integrals.

title: Calculus II
description: Calculus II: techniques of integration, applications of integration, sequences, series and Taylor series.
learning_outcomes: Apply integration techniques; test series for convergence; build Taylor approximations.

title: Multivariate Calculus
description: Multivariate calculus: vectors, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus including Green's and Stokes' theorems.
learning_outcomes: Compute partial derivatives and multiple integrals; apply vector calculus theorems.

title: Linear Algebra
description: Linear algebra: systems of equations, matrices, vector spaces, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and orthogonality.
learning_outcomes: Solve linear systems; work with vector spaces; compute eigenvalues; prove basic results.

title: Differential Equations
description: Differential equations: first-order equations, linear second-order equations, systems of equations, Laplace transforms and qualitative analysis.
learning_outcomes: Solve ODEs analytically; analyse systems qualitatively; model physical systems.

title: Discrete Mathematics
description: Discrete mathematics: logic, proofs, sets, relations, functions, combinatorics, recurrence relations and graph theory.
learning_outcomes: Construct proofs; solve combinatorial and recurrence problems; reason about graphs.

title: Probability
description: Probability theory: axioms, random variables, joint distributions, expectation, limit theorems and an introduction to stochastic processes.
learning_outcomes: Compute probabilities and expectations; apply the law of large numbers and CLT.

title: Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
description: Introductory program design using Python with a required lab. Data-driven design, functions, conditionals, lists, iteration, recursion and testing.
learning_outcomes: Design programs systematically from data definitions; write tested functions; use recursion and lists.

title: Program Design and Implementation 1
description: Program design and implementation 1 with lab: object-oriented design in Java, classes, interfaces, inheritance, testing and abstraction. Data structures are covered mainly in CS 2700.
learning_outcomes: Design class hierarchies; write unit tests; apply abstraction and encapsulation in Java.

title: Program Design and Implementation 2
description: Program design and implementation 2 with lab: larger-scale software design, design patterns, modularity, and team projects.
learning_outcomes: Apply design patterns; build multi-module applications; collaborate using version control.

title: Discrete Structures
description: Discrete structures: logic, sets, proof by induction, counting, probability, graphs, and modular arithmetic for computer science.
learning_outcomes: Write inductive proofs; solve counting and probability problems; reason about graphs.

title: Data Structures and Analysis
description: Data structures and analysis with lab: lists, stacks, queues, trees, heaps, hash tables, graphs and asymptotic analysis.
learning_outcomes: Implement and analyse standard data structures; select structures for performance.

title: Algorithms and Data
description: Algorithms and data: divide and conquer, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, graph algorithms and intractability.
learning_outcomes: Design and analyse algorithms; prove correctness; identify NP-hard problems.

title: Computer Systems
description: Computer systems: C programming, machine representation, assembly, memory management, processes, threads and file systems.
learning_outcomes: Program in C; explain memory and process abstractions; write basic concurrent code.

title: Theory of Computation
description: Theory of computation: automata, regular and context-free languages, Turing machines, computability and complexity.
learning_outcomes: Build automata; prove undecidability; reason about complexity classes.

title: Programming Languages
description: Programming languages: semantics, interpreters, type systems and language design.
learning_outcomes: Implement interpreters; reason about type safety and semantics.

title: Logic and Computation
description: Logic and computation: propositional and predicate logic, formal reasoning about programs, and theorem proving.
learning_outcomes: Prove program properties formally; use a theorem prover.

title: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
description: Mathematical foundations of AI: linear algebra, probability and optimisation applied to machine-learning models.
learning_outcomes: Apply linear algebra and probability to ML; implement gradient-based optimisation.

title: Principles of Microeconomics
description: Principles of microeconomics: markets, supply and demand, elasticity, firm behaviour, competition and market failure.
learning_outcomes: Analyse markets with supply and demand; compare market structures; assess policy.

title: Principles of Macroeconomics
description: Principles of macroeconomics: national income, unemployment, inflation, growth, money and stabilisation policy.
learning_outcomes: Interpret macro data; use AD-AS models; explain monetary and fiscal policy.

title: Microeconomic Theory
description: Microeconomic theory with calculus: consumer and producer theory, equilibrium, game theory and welfare.
learning_outcomes: Solve optimisation problems; analyse equilibrium and strategic behaviour.

title: Macroeconomic Theory
description: Macroeconomic theory: growth, business cycles, IS-LM, open economy and policy analysis.
learning_outcomes: Build macro models; evaluate policy using formal frameworks.

title: Statistics for Economists
description: Statistics for economists: probability, estimation, hypothesis testing and simple regression using economic data.
learning_outcomes: Run hypothesis tests; estimate simple regressions; interpret results.

title: Applied Econometrics
description: Applied econometrics: multiple regression, specification, heteroskedasticity, and an applied data project. Limited coverage of instrumental variables.
learning_outcomes: Estimate and diagnose regression models; complete an applied project.

title: Foundations of Psychology

learning_outcomes: Explain neural mechanisms of behaviour; evaluate biological research.

title: Developmental Psychology
